# Changing a cross-process contract

The rule: **if a type crosses a process boundary, it lives in `forge-platform-wire`.**
Never hand-roll a struct another process parses. The compile failure in every consumer is
the point — it's the mechanism that keeps the fleet in lockstep.

The facts in this skill are atom blocks rendered from `forge-facts` at `harness build`; the
sweep checks each against the tree. A block that reads wrong is a fact that moved: fix the
atom, never the prose here.

## First: identify which contract you're touching

There are five, and they have different blast radii and different rollout rules.

### 1. `forge-platform-wire` types — compile-fenced

<!-- fact: platform/wire-types-inventory -->
forge-platform-wire defines the fleet-loop wire structs ExecutionEnvelope, StatusReport, EnvelopesResponse, RoutingTableResponse, Route, InstanceStatus and MetricsSnapshot, among its other pub types.

The structs the CP, agent, edge and runtime exchange on the fleet loop live in `forge-platform-wire/src`: `ExecutionEnvelope` (envelope.rs), `EnvelopesResponse` and `StatusReport` (control_plane.rs), `RoutingTableResponse` and `Route` (routing_table.rs), `InstanceStatus` and `MetricsSnapshot`. Changing one fails compilation in every consumer, which is the point: a type that crosses a process boundary is never hand-rolled.

They are not the whole crate. At extraction it carried 48 pub structs and enums, among them `EngineSlot`, `TenantCert`, `FleetTokenClaims`, `SigningKeyCert`, `AuthenticatorCatalog`, the unit-pin types and the changelog-revert types.

<!-- fact: platform/wire-consumers -->
Six repos path-depend on forge-platform-wire: forge-runtime, forge-agent, forge-control-plane, forge-edge, forge-cli and forge-lang (forge-lang-engine).

`forge-platform-wire = { path = ... }` appears in the root `Cargo.toml` of forge-runtime, forge-agent, forge-control-plane, forge-edge and forge-cli, and in `forge-lang/crates/forge-lang-engine/Cargo.toml`. A wire change is checked against all six before it merges:

```bash
for r in forge-runtime forge-agent forge-control-plane forge-edge forge-cli forge-lang; do
  (cd "$r" && cargo check --tests --locked) || echo "BROKE: $r"
done
```

forge-runtime needs its `--features adapters` for the check to mean anything. Consumer CI checks out forge-platform-wire from its default branch, so consumer PRs are red until the wire change is on main.

This is the safest kind — a change breaks the build everywhere it matters. Wire-shape
regression tests in the crate gate every CI run.

### 2. CP HTTP surfaces — *not* fully fenced

<!-- fact: platform/cp-admin-api-hand-rolled-json -->
The CP's /admin API is hand-rolled JSON: its handlers define local Serialize structs and forge-cp builds bodies with serde_json::json!, so no compile fence covers it.

The operator admin API (`/admin/workspaces`, `/admin/nodes`, `/admin/assignments`, `/admin/routing-table`, `/admin/usage`) is served from `forge-control-plane/src/admin/`, whose handlers answer with structs defined beside them rather than forge-platform-wire types. The `forge-cp` binary talks plain HTTP to it and builds request bodies with `serde_json::json!`, reading answers as `serde_json::Value`. Nothing catches a mismatch at compile time: change both sides in one commit and exercise the path.

Nothing catches a mismatch there at compile time. Change both sides in the same commit and
test the path.

<!-- fact: platform/cp-supported-versions-header -->
The CP picks the envelope wire version for GET /node/:id/envelopes from the agent's X-Forge-Supported-Versions header, defaulting to v1.

The agent-facing CP surface is `GET /node/:id/envelopes` and `POST /node/:id/status` (`src/routes.rs`), both carrying forge-platform-wire types. `pick_wire_version` reads `X-Forge-Supported-Versions`, a comma-separated list of u32; with no header it answers v1 for old agents, otherwise the highest version in both the agent's set and `1..=SUPPORTED_ENVELOPE_VERSION`. An agent on the old shape must keep being served, or its node's workspaces stop converging.

### 3. Secrets broker UDS protocol — version-pinned, fails closed

<!-- fact: platform/broker-uds-protocol-v1 -->
The secrets broker speaks newline-JSON on /run/forge-secrets.sock; every request carries v: 1, a mismatch is refused with the protocol error, and it has nine ops.

`forge-secrets` listens on `/run/forge-secrets.sock` by default, one newline-delimited JSON request and response per line (`src/protocol.rs`). Every request carries `v`, which must equal `WIRE_PROTOCOL_VERSION` (1); anything else is refused with error code `protocol` (`error_codes::PROTOCOL`), so a stale client fails at its first message.

The ops, tagged by `op`: `GetDek`, `Sign`, `Verify`, `Encrypt`, `CloneDek`, `DeleteDek`, `GetLakeKey`, `DestroyLakeKey`, `ListLakeKeys`. A new op or optional field needs no bump; an incompatible change is a flag day, because broker and every client (runtime, `forge-cp`, the CP) must ship together.

Bumping the version is a **flag-day**: broker and every client (runtime, `forge-cp`) must
ship together, because old clients get hard-rejected. Prefer additive optional fields.

### 4. The WIT component ABI — customer-facing, effectively frozen

<!-- fact: platform/wit-package-forge-platform-0-2-0 -->
forge-runtime/wit/forge.wit declares package forge:platform@0.2.0, and forge-sdk-v2 generates its bindings from ../forge-runtime/wit by relative path.

The Component Model contract is `forge-runtime/wit/forge.wit`, `package forge:platform@0.2.0;`. `forge-sdk-v2/src/lib.rs` runs `wit_bindgen::generate!` against `path: "../forge-runtime/wit"`, so an edit there changes the ABI for every deployed guest. Additive items are usually safe; changing or removing a signature breaks deployed guests and belongs in a new package version.

Changing it changes the ABI for every deployed customer wasm module, not just ours.
Additive world/interface items are usually safe; changing or removing an existing signature
breaks already-deployed guests. Treat a breaking change as a new package version, not an
edit.

### 5. The routing table — one-way, poll-based

<!-- fact: platform/edge-polls-routing-every-3s -->
forge-edge polls the CP's /admin/routing-table every --reload-secs, 3 in the deployed units (binary default 5), swaps an ArcSwap, and keeps the previous table on a failed poll.

The edge reads `GET <cp-url>/admin/routing-table` every `--reload-secs` (`FORGE_EDGE_RELOAD_SECS`). The binary's default is 5; both systemd units in forge-platform-operations (`forge-edge.service.tmpl`, `forge-edge-internal.service.tmpl`) pass `--reload-secs 3`. Each good poll swaps the table in an `arc_swap::ArcSwap`; a failed poll logs and keeps the previous table, so the edge degrades rather than dies. The edge never writes routing state.

<!-- fact: platform/cp-stale-gate-30s -->
The CP marks a route unhealthy when its node was last seen more than DEFAULT_STALE_THRESHOLD_SECS (30) ago; the edge has no stale gate of its own.

`DEFAULT_STALE_THRESHOLD_SECS = 30` lives in `forge-platform-wire/src/routing_table.rs`. The CP's `build_routing_table` takes it as `stale_threshold_secs` and overrides `healthy` to false for every route on a node unseen that long, so the edge stops dialing a dead box within one reload window. The edge carries no threshold of its own; do not reimplement the gate there. `/admin/routing-table` accepts `?stale_secs=` to override it.

Edge never writes routing state, and the stale-gate is **the CP's job** — do not
reimplement it in the edge.

## Landing order

Dependencies flow `platform-wire → {runtime, agent, control-plane, edge}`, so:

1. **`forge-platform-wire` first.** Add the field/variant. Prefer additive and
   `#[serde(default)]` so a mixed-version fleet keeps parsing.
2. **Build every consumer against your local sibling** before pushing anything:
   ```bash
   for r in forge-runtime forge-agent forge-control-plane forge-edge; do
     (cd "$r" && cargo check --tests --locked) || echo "BROKE: $r"
   done
   ```
   Use the `forge-build` skill for the correct per-repo command — `forge-runtime` needs its feature
   set, and a bare `cargo check` there is misleading.
3. **Merge `forge-platform-wire`, then consumers.** Consumer CI checks out
   `forge-platform-wire` from *its* default branch, so consumer PRs go red until the wire
   change is on `main`. That ordering is expected, not a failure.
4. **Deploy in dependency order**, and only via the fleet manifest — see the `forge-release` skill.

## Rollout across a running fleet

<!-- fact: ops/forge-deploy-is-pull-based -->
Nodes converge themselves: forge-reconciler.timer fires every 60 s, fetches manifest.yaml and swaps any binary that differs.

forge nodes converge themselves. `forge-reconciler.timer` fires every 60s on each node, fetches `forge-platform-operations/manifest.yaml` over the GitHub API, compares `versions:` against `/etc/forge-versions/<crate>`, and atomic-swaps any binary that differs (sha256-verified, prior copy kept at `<bin>.prev`).

The operator edits the manifest, `just bump <crate> vX.Y.Z`, rather than pushing binaries. `forge-runtime` is service-less, so its rollout lands gradually as workspaces cold-start.

**How to apply:** two consequences that bite. (1) `just rollback` is SSH-side and does NOT edit the manifest, so the reconciler pulls the bad version forward again within 60s; always follow a rollback by bumping the manifest back. (2) Nodes poll independently, so mixed versions are always live for at least one cycle; a non-additive wire change is an outage in that window. Version 1 warned that `runbooks/deploy.md` still documented the push model; AR-4 retired that section and the runbook pins this atom.

Nodes converge independently, so **there is always a window where mixed versions are
live.** A non-additive change is a real outage in that window.

- Additive + `serde(default)` → safe.
- Removing or renaming a field → two releases. Ship readers that tolerate both, converge the
  whole fleet, then remove the old writer.
- Agent ↔ CP: agents poll and push continuously. An agent on the old shape must not be
  rejected by a new CP, or that node's workspaces stop converging.
- Edge ↔ CP: edge fails its poll → it keeps serving the last good `Arc<RoutingTable>`.
  Degraded but not dead. Don't make a parse failure fatal.

## Anti-patterns that will fail review

- Reconstructing a wire type locally instead of importing `forge-platform-wire`.
- Adding app-level auth or TLS to the edge → runtime hop (fenced at the network layer by design).
- Having the CP read or write customer data, or run wasm.
- Borrowing a customer's or git-pusher's credential for a converge write — platform-tier
  writes self-sign with a broker-derived `fr_p_` HMAC:

<!-- fact: platform/bearer-prefixes-and-ttls -->
Bearer prefixes: fr_u_ user access token (1 h), fr_s_ refresh token (30 d), fr_p_ platform HMAC with a 60 s replay window.

Opaque tokens are `fr_<tier>_<ws alias>_<rand>` (39 chars), parsed in `forge-types/crates/forge-types/src/service/token.rs`: tier `u` is User, `s` is Service. forge-storage's login and refresh mint the access token at the user tier with `DEFAULT_ACCESS_TTL_SECS = 3600` and the refresh token at the service tier with `DEFAULT_REFRESH_TTL_SECS = 30 * 24 * 3600`, so `fr_u_` is a 1 h access token and `fr_s_` a 30 d refresh token.

Platform-tier writes carry `fr_p_` (`PLATFORM_BEARER_PREFIX` in `forge-runtime-auth/src/platform.rs`), an HMAC the broker signs, checked within `PLATFORM_SIG_WINDOW_SECS = 60`. A converge write self-signs this way; it never borrows a customer's or a git pusher's credential.

- The runtime calling KMS directly instead of going through the broker.

## Verify

```bash
cd forge-platform-wire && cargo test --tests --locked   # wire-shape regression tests
```

<!-- fact: platform/fleet-check-script -->
forge-platform-architecture/graph/tools/fleet-check.sh is the drift gate as a thin wrapper over forge-facts: facts sweep against the working root, then facts judge --strict and facts render --check over every document and runbook this repo renders.

`bash forge-platform-architecture/graph/tools/fleet-check.sh` runs three steps, one direction: `facts sweep` re-runs every atom's verify against the working root (`FORGE_FLEET_ROOT`, else the sibling layout; forge-facts at `FORGE_FACTS_ROOT`, else beside the root), `facts judge --strict` refuses on any pin in ARCHITECTURE.md, BOUNDARIES.md, TRUST.md, STANDING.md, README.md or a runbook whose verdict is not holds, and `facts render --check` refuses a block that is not the render of its atom. Exit 0 means every pinned atom holds and every block is current; non-zero names the keys; 2 means the gate could not run. Run it after a cross-process change; a boundary change rather than a field change also needs an ADR in `forge-platform-architecture/decisions/`. Version 1 ran the hand-authored graph's reconcilers, which retired with the graph: forge-graph holds the code graph now.

If you added a cross-process field, `forge-platform-architecture` may need a matching
edit — and if you changed a boundary rather than a field, that needs an ADR in
`forge-platform-architecture/decisions/`, numbered next in sequence.
